Review target: `14704cf6..267d950f`

`low effort → 1 diff pass → no verify → ≤4 findings`

## Turn 1 — read

One tool call: read the unified diff (`git diff @{upstream}...HEAD; git diff HEAD`
to cover both committed and uncommitted changes, or `git diff main...HEAD` /
the target passed as an argument). Skip test/fixture
hunks (`test/`, `spec/`, `__tests__/`, `*_test.*`, `*.test.*`,
`fixtures/`, `testdata/`) — test-file changes are not reviewed at this level.
No subagents, no full-file reads.

## Turn 2 — findings

Flag runtime-correctness bugs visible from the hunk alone: inverted/wrong
condition, off-by-one, null/undefined deref where adjacent lines show the value
can be absent, removed guard, falsy-zero check, missing `await`,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in a catch that should propagate.
Also flag — still from the hunk alone — new code that duplicates an existing
helper visible in the diff context, and dead code the diff leaves behind.

Do **not** flag style, naming, perf, missing tests, or anything outside the
hunk.

Output at most **4 findings**, most-severe first, one line each:
`path/to/file.ext:123 — what's wrong and the concrete failure`. If nothing
qualifies, output exactly `(none)`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available.

crates/core/src/extractor/body_facts.rs:288-299 — `arguments` check uses `root_unresolved_references()`, which only holds references unresolved at the root scope. If the function is nested in another scope that declares its own `arguments`, or the reference is resolved against an enclosing function's `arguments`, it is missed. It can also be set by an unrelated `arguments` elsewhere in the file. A component that reads `arguments[0]` can therefore be reported as fully read (`handed_on` false), or an unrelated one wrongly marked unknown. The check should look at references within this function's own scope.

crates/core/src/extractor/body_facts.rs:510-549 — The new `is_read` allow-list leaves out common read-only parents, so any use of the props object under them now sets `handed_on` and the component becomes unknown. Parents missing from the list include `UnaryExpression` (`!props`, `typeof` is intentionally handed on), `ParenthesizedExpression`, `TSNonNullExpression`, `TSAsExpression` and `TSSatisfiesExpression`. The commit message says `props!.x` is recorded, so `(props as P).x` or `(props).x` would regress from complete to unknown. If the allow-list sits behind a parenthesis or TS-wrapper unwrapping step, that step is not visible in this hunk.

crates/core/src/extractor/body_facts.rs:515-548 — `ForInStatement`, `ForOfStatement`, `CallExpression` arguments and `TaggedTemplateExpression` are also absent. Whether they hand the object on is the intended behavior. `ForStatement` and `NewExpression` are listed as reads, while `CallExpression` is not, so `new Foo(props)` counts as a read and `foo(props)` hands on. That looks inconsistent, because both pass the object to unknown code.
